name: DNS Server Directory
description: Lists the UDP / TCP / DoT / DoH endpoints of popular public DNS resolvers; search and filter by region, protocol and address family.

hints.query: Accepts a provider name (AliDNS, Cloudflare) or an address (1.1.1.1); the text search combines with the region, protocol and address-family filters.
hints.output: All endpoints are listed by default; typing or picking a filter narrows the list instantly. Every address can be copied on its own, and the "Test" column jumps to DNS Lookup with that endpoint prefilled.
hints.note: Data comes from a built-in snapshot — nothing is sent over the network. Addresses are the general public endpoints of each provider; always confirm against the provider's own documentation.

faq.q: Why does the same IP show up twice?
faq.a: UDP and TCP are two independent query channels. UDP is fast but can drop packets, while TCP is slower yet carries larger responses — which DNSSEC records especially need. Since providers offer both, each one gets its own row.

faq.q: What is the difference between DoT and DoH?
faq.a: Both are encrypted DNS channels. DoT runs TLS on port 853; DoH runs HTTPS on port 443, so it still works on networks that only allow 443. Both are far harder for middleboxes to interfere with than plaintext queries.

faq.q: What does the "Hostname" address family mean?
faq.a: DoT and DoH endpoints are usually given as hostnames (such as dns.alidns.com) that the system resolves before connecting. "IPv4" and "IPv6" are address literals given directly.
It opens DNS Lookup with that endpoint's protocol and address prefilled in the custom server list, so a real query is one click away.
